TOKENAMUN  what-if: mcp-to-cli

put an MCP server behind a CLI instead of exposing its tool schemas
Session carry-fixture, 8 API calls

Observed
  mcp tool results                                        0   [observed]
  mcp result content                                    0 B   [observed]
  session preamble, a ceiling on the category        30,001   [observed]
  cost of carrying the preamble                      49,501   [observed]

Not measurable from this data
  The saving lives in tool-schema size, and tool schemas are not in the
  transcript. The observed session preamble is a ceiling on the whole
  category, not a measurement of the schemas inside it. This session made
  no MCP calls, which is not the same as having no MCP cost: a connected
  server's schemas sit in the preamble on every call whether anything
  calls it or not, and a transcript cannot tell an unused server from an
  absent one. Reporting 0% here would be a claim, and it would be wrong in
  the expensive direction. To measure it, run the same opening prompt with
  the server connected and disconnected and compare the first call's
  prompt size: that difference is observed. `tokenamun compare` is the
  command for it.

Unknown
  - schema_tokens: not observable from a transcript at all.
  - tools_available: only tools that were used appear; the ones that
    merely occupied context do not.
  - task_success: not observable from this data. An agent that fails the
    task consumes the fewest tokens of all, so a reduction is not an
    improvement.
